readings.title: Purification After Childbirth
readings.subtitle: Separation and Offerings
readings.text: [Leviticus 12:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’el, saying, ‘When a woman conceives and bears a male child, then she shall be unclean seven days; as in the days of her separation for her infirmity she is unclean.</dq> [3] <dq>‘And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin is circumcised.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And she remains in the blood of cleansing thirty-three days. She does not touch what is set-apart, nor come into the set-apart place, until the days of her cleansing are completed.</dq> [5] <dq>‘But if she bears a female child, then she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her separation, and she remains in the blood of cleansing sixty-six days.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And when the days of her cleansing are completed, for a son or for a daughter, she brings to the priest a lamb of the first year as a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering, to the door of the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And he shall bring it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood. This is the Torah for her who has borne a male or a female.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And if she is not able to bring a lamb, then she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a burnt offering and the other as a sin offering. And the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.’”</dq>

readings.title: The Laws of Skin Afflictions
readings.subtitle: Identifying the Plague
readings.text: [Leviticus 13:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying, [2] <dq>“When a man has on the skin of his flesh a swelling, a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes on the skin of his flesh like a leprous sore, then he shall be brought to Aharon the priest or to one of his sons the priests.</dq> [3] <dq>“And the priest shall look at the sore on the skin of the flesh. And if the hair on the sore has turned white, and the sore appears to be deeper than the skin of his flesh, it is a leprous sore. And the priest shall look at him, and pronounce him unclean.</dq> [4] <dq>“But if the bright spot is white on the skin of his flesh, and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, then the priest shall shut up the sore seven days.</dq> [5] <dq>“And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day. And see, if the sore appears to stay, and the sore has not spread on the skin, then the priest shall shut him up another seven days.</dq> [6] <dq>“And the priest shall look at him again the seventh day. And see, if the sore has faded, and the sore has not spread on the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. It is a scab, and he shall wash his garments and be clean.</dq> [7] <dq>“But if the scab spreads further over the skin, after he has been seen by the priest for his cleansing, he shall be seen by the priest again.</dq> [8] <dq>“And the priest shall look, and see, if the scab has spread on the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is leprosy.</dq> [9] <dq>“When the sore of leprosy is on a man, then he shall be brought to the priest.</dq> [10] <dq>“And the priest shall look, and see, if the swelling is white on the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,</dq> [11] <dq>it is an old leprosy on the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. He does not shut him up, for he is unclean.</dq> [12] <dq>“And if leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the one who has the sore, from his head to his foot, wherever the priest looks,</dq> [13] <dq>then the priest shall look, and see, if the leprosy has covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce the sore clean. It has all turned white. He is clean.</dq> [14] <dq>“But on the day raw flesh appears on him, he is unclean.</dq> [15] <dq>“And the priest shall look at the raw flesh and pronounce him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean, it is leprosy.</dq> [16] <dq>“Or if the raw flesh changes and turns white again, he shall come to the priest.</dq> [17] <dq>“And the priest shall look at him, and see, if the sore has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce the sore clean. He is clean.</dq> [18] <dq>“And when the body has a boil on its skin and it is healed,</dq> [19] <dq>and in the place of the boil there comes a white swelling or a bright spot, reddish-white, then it shall be seen by the priest.</dq> [20] <dq>“And the priest shall look, and see, if it appears deeper than the skin, and its hair has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a leprous sore which has broken out of the boil.</dq> [21] <dq>“But if the priest looks at it, and sees no white hairs in it, and it is not deeper than the skin, but has faded, then the priest shall shut him up seven days.</dq> [22] <dq>“And if it spreads further over the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a sore.</dq> [23] <dq>“But if the bright spot stays in one place, and has not spread, it is the scar of the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.</dq> [24] <dq>“Or if the body receives a burn on its skin by fire, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white or white,</dq> [25] <dq>then the priest shall look at it. And see, if the hair of the bright spot has turned white, and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy broken out of the burn. And the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a leprous sore.</dq> [26] <dq>“But if the priest looks at it, and sees no white hair in the bright spot, and it is not deeper than the skin, but has faded, then the priest shall shut him up seven days.</dq> [27] <dq>“And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day. If it spreads further over the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a leprous sore.</dq> [28] <dq>“But if the bright spot stays in one place, and has not spread on the skin, but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn. And the priest shall pronounce him clean, for it is the scar from the burn.</dq> [29] <dq>“And if a man or woman has a sore on the head or on the beard,</dq> [30] <dq>then the priest shall look at the sore. And see, if it appears deeper than the skin, and there is in it thin yellow hair, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a scale, a leprosy of the head or beard.</dq> [31] <dq>“But if the priest looks at the sore of the scale, and sees that it does not appear deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then the priest shall shut up the one who has the sore of the scale seven days.</dq> [32] <dq>“And on the seventh day the priest shall look at the sore. And see, if the scale has not spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the scale does not appear deeper than the skin,</dq> [33] <dq>then he shall shave himself, but the scale he does not shave. And the priest shall shut up the one who has the scale another seven days.</dq> [34] <dq>“And on the seventh day the priest shall look at the scale. And see, if the scale has not spread over the skin, and does not appear deeper than the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. And he shall wash his garments, and be clean.</dq> [35] <dq>“But if the scale spreads further over the skin after his cleansing,</dq> [36] <dq>then the priest shall look at him. And see, if the scale has spread over the skin, the priest need not seek for yellow hair. He is unclean.</dq> [37] <dq>“But if the scale appears to be at a standstill, and there is black hair grown up in it, the scale has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.</dq> [38] <dq>“And if a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin of the body, white bright spots,</dq> [39] <dq>then the priest shall look. And see, if the bright spots on the skin of the body are dull white, it is a white spot that grows on the skin. He is clean.</dq> [40] <dq>“And if a man loses the hair of his head, he is bald. He is clean.</dq> [41] <dq>“And if the hair of his head has fallen from his forehead, he is bald on the forehead. He is clean.</dq> [42] <dq>“And if there is on the bald head or bald forehead a reddish-white sore, it is leprosy breaking out on his bald head or his bald forehead.</dq> [43] <dq>“Then the priest shall look at it. And see, if the swelling of the sore is reddish-white on his bald head or on his bald forehead, as the appearance of leprosy on the skin of the body,</dq> [44] <dq>he is a leprous man. He is unclean. The priest shall unhesitatingly pronounce him unclean. His sore is on his head.</dq> [45] <dq>“As for the leper who has the sore, his garments shall be torn, and his head uncovered, and he shall cover his upper lip, and cry, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’</dq> [46] <dq>“He is unclean. All the days he has the sore he shall be unclean. He is unclean, and he dwells alone, his dwelling place is outside the camp.</dq>

readings.title: Leprosy in Garments
readings.subtitle: Inspection and Judgement
readings.text: [Leviticus 13:47] <dq>“And when a garment has a leprous sore on it, whether it is a woollen garment or a linen garment,</dq> [48] <dq>whether it is in the warp or in the woof, of linen or wool, or in leather or in any leather work,</dq> [49] <dq>and the sore is greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the leather, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any leather object, it is a leprous sore and shall be shown to the priest.</dq> [50] <dq>“And the priest shall look at the sore, and shut up the sore seven days.</dq> [51] <dq>“And he shall look at the sore on the seventh day. If the sore has spread in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in leather, in any work that is made of leather, the sore is an active leprosy. It is unclean.</dq> [52] <dq>“And he shall burn the garment, or the warp, or the woof, in wool or in linen, or any leather object in which the sore is. For it is an active leprosy, it is burned with fire.</dq> [53] <dq>“But if the priest looks, and sees that the sore has not spread in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any leather object,</dq> [54] <dq>then the priest shall command that they wash that in which the sore is, and he shall shut it up another seven days.</dq> [55] <dq>“And the priest shall look at the sore after it has been washed. And see, if the sore has not changed its appearance, though the sore has not spread, it is unclean, you burn it in the fire. It is a decay in its inside or on its outside.</dq> [56] <dq>“And if the priest looks, and sees that the sore has faded after washing it, then he shall tear it out of the garment, or out of the leather, or out of the warp, or out of the woof.</dq> [57] <dq>“And if it is still seen in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any leather object, it is a spreading leprosy. You burn with fire that in which the sore is.</dq> [58] <dq>“And the garment, or the warp, or the woof, or any leather object which you wash, and the sore has departed from it, shall be washed a second time, and shall be clean.</dq> [59] <dq>“This is the Torah of the leprous sore in a garment of wool or linen, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any leather object, to pronounce it clean or to pronounce it unclean.”</dq>

readings.title: The Ritual of Cleansing
readings.subtitle: Offerings for Restoration
readings.text: [Leviticus 14:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“This shall be the Torah of the leper for the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought to the priest.</dq> [3] <dq>“And the priest shall go out of the camp, and the priest shall look. And see, if the leprosy is healed in the leper,</dq> [4] <dq>then the priest shall command to take for him who is to be cleansed two living and clean birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.</dq> [5] <dq>“And the priest shall command that one of the birds be killed in an earthen vessel over running water.</dq> [6] <dq>“As for the living bird, he takes it, the cedar wood and the scarlet and the hyssop, and dips them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water.</dq> [7] <dq>“And he shall sprinkle it seven times on him who is to be cleansed from the leprosy, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let the living bird loose in the open field.</dq> [8] <dq>“And he who is to be cleansed shall wash his garments, and shave off all his hair and wash himself in water, and shall be clean. And after that he comes into the camp, but shall stay outside his tent seven days.</dq> [9] <dq>“And on the seventh day it shall be that he shaves all the hair off his head and his beard and his eyebrows, even all his hair he shaves off. And he shall wash his garments and wash his body in water, and shall be clean.</dq> [10] <dq>“And on the eighth day he takes two male lambs, perfect ones, and one ewe lamb of the first year, perfect one, and three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one log of oil.</dq> [11] <dq>“And the priest who pronounces him clean shall present the man who is to be made clean, and those offerings, before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.</dq> [12] <dq>“And the priest shall take one male lamb and bring it as a guilt offering, and the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [13] <dq>“And he shall slaughter the lamb in the place where he slaughters the sin offering and the burnt offering, in a set-apart place. For the guilt offering is the priest’s, like the sin offering, it is most set-apart.</dq> [14] <dq>“And the priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering, and the priest shall put it on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.</dq> [15] <dq>“And the priest shall take some of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.</dq> [16] <dq>“And the priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [17] <dq>“And of the rest of the oil in his hand, the priest puts some on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the blood of the guilt offering.</dq> [18] <dq>“And the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he puts on the head of him who is to be cleansed. And the priest shall make atonement for him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [19] <dq>“And the priest shall prepare the sin offering, and make atonement for him who is to be cleansed from his uncleanness. And afterward he slaughters the burnt offering.</dq> [20] <dq>“And the priest shall offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.</dq> [21] <dq>“But if he is poor and his hand is not able to get so much, then he shall take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil,</dq> [22] <dq>“and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, such as his hand is able to get. And the one shall be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.</dq> [23] <dq>“And he shall bring them to the priest on the eighth day for his cleansing, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [24] <dq>“And the priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and the priest shall wave them a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [25] <dq>“And he shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.</dq> [26] <dq>“And the priest shall pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.</dq> [27] <dq>“And the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“And the priest shall put some of the oil that is in his hand on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of the right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the place of the blood of the guilt offering.</dq> [29] <dq>“And the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he puts on the head of him who is to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [30] <dq>“And he shall prepare one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, such as his hand is able to get,</dq> [31] <dq>“that which his hand is able to get: the one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, with the grain offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him who is to be cleansed before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [32] <dq>“This is the Torah for him in whom is a leprous sore, whose hand is not able to get the offering for his cleansing.”</dq>
